question: Which constitutional authority is appointed by the President of India under Article 76 of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Attorney General of India**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Attorney General of India** is appointed by the President of India under Article 76 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Attorney General is the highest law officer in the country and serves as the chief legal advisor to the government of India.
 
• He/she represents the government of India in legal matters and performs duties of a legal character as assigned by the President.
 
• The Attorney General has the right to participate in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament but does not have the right to vote.
 
• The position of the Attorney General is not a full-time engagement, and the person holding the office can practice privately as well, provided it does not conflict with the duties of the office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Chief Election Commissioner** is appointed by the President of India but is not related to Article 76.
 
• The **Comptroller & Auditor General of India** is also appointed by the President but under Article 148.
 
• The **Chief Justice of India** is appointed by the President under Article 124.
 
• The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and can be removed by the President at any time.
 
• The appointment of the Attorney General is usually for a term of three years, which can be extended.
